symptom: congestion-driven routing DRCs with clean placement density

first_checks.check: Run congestion map and identify hotspots
Verify pin access in hotspot regions
Review macro placement for tight clusters
Check power grid density in congested areas

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If congestion map shows hotspots aligned with specific macros, check macro placement spacing
If hotspots are concentrated at power ring edges, verify power grid width and pitch
If hotspots are random and widespread, run global placement with higher congestion weight

common_root_causes.cause: macro placement too tight
power grid under-design
pin access blocked by fill or other macros
global placement algorithm not accounting for routing congestion

classic_trap: Blame global placement when the root cause is macro placement or power grid design
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: more routing layers reduce congestion severity, but power grid density requirements increase

first_checks.check: Check timing report for top failing paths and their clock domains
Verify clock latency and skew in failing clock domains
Review wireload models for accuracy against actual routing
Inspect clock network for missing buffers or excessive fanout

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If all failing paths share one common clock domain, check clock latency in that domain
If failing paths are in the same hierarchy and share long wires, verify wireload model vs actual routing capacitance
If failing paths are spread across unrelated hierarchies but share a common clock root, check clock tree insertion delay

common_root_causes.cause: clock network delays due to excessive fanout or missing buffers
wireload model overestimation for global routes
placement congestion forcing detours in critical paths
library characterization mismatch for late-stage timing

classic_trap: Optimize combinational logic when the real issue is clock network latency or wireload modeling
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: more buffer stages in clock network make latency more sensitive to fanout

first_checks.check: Check hold margins on failing paths in timing report
Verify clock skew between launch and capture flops in failing paths
first_checks.why_first: rules out clock skew as root cause

first_checks.check: Inspect fanout and net capacitance on short paths
first_checks.why_first: rules out excessive fanout on short nets

first_checks.check: Review clock gating cells on failing paths for excessive delay
first_checks.why_first: rules out clock gating induced hold issues

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If all failing paths share one common clock-gating cell, check its insertion delay
If failing paths are short and local to a single hierarchy, verify fanout and net capacitance
If failing paths spread across unrelated hierarchies but share launch/capture clock domains, check clock skew between domains

common_root_causes.cause: clock skew between launch and capture flops
clock gating cells with insufficient delay buffering
excessive fanout on short nets in critical paths
library hold margins too tight for process variation

classic_trap: Add hold buffers on data paths when the real issue is clock skew or clock gating delay
node_era_note: 28nm: more hold issues due to fewer clock buffer stages; 7nm-and-below: finer clock network reduces skew but increases gating complexity

first_checks.check: Run IR-drop analysis and map to failing timing paths
Verify power grid resistance and voltage drop in failing regions
Check timing at low VDD corners for same paths
Review power consumption of logic in failing regions

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If timing fails only at low VDD corners but passes at nominal, check IR-drop values in those regions
If failing paths are clustered in high-current-density regions, verify power grid width and via count
If IR-drop is uniform but timing fails only in specific logic blocks, check decap placement in those blocks

common_root_causes.cause: power grid resistance too high for current demand
high current density in switching logic
VDD too low for timing at low corners
insufficient decap in critical timing paths
library characterization not accounting for IR-drop

classic_trap: Blame timing optimization when the root cause is IR-drop in power grid
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: finer power grids and more decap options, but higher current density

symptom: clock skew / CTS divergence (sinks missing insertion-delay targets)

first_checks.check: Check clock latency report for sinks with worst insertion delay
Verify clock tree topology for imbalanced branches
Inspect buffer sizes and fanout in failing clock branches
Review clock constraints and exceptions for failing sinks

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If all failing sinks share a common clock branch, check buffer sizes and wire lengths in that branch
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: buffer sizing or wire length issue in branch

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If failing sinks are in the same region, check for local congestion blocking ideal clock tree routing
If failing sinks are spread across chip but share a common clock root, verify clock tree synthesis constraints
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: clock tree synthesis constraints too loose

common_root_causes.cause: buffer sizing not optimal for clock tree branches
clock tree topology not balanced for all sinks
congestion blocking ideal clock tree routing
clock constraints not accounting for process variation

classic_trap: Add more buffers to clock tree when the real issue is topology imbalance or congestion blocking
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: more automated CTS with stricter skew targets, less manual topology tweaking

symptom: LVS mismatch: missing / shorted / open nets

first_checks.check: Run LVS and categorize mismatches by type (missing/short/open)
Verify netlist vs layout connectivity for failing nets
first_checks.why_first: rules out netlist vs layout discrepancies

first_checks.check: Check DRC hotspots in regions with LVS mismatches
Review fill cell insertion in failing regions
first_checks.why_first: rules out fill-induced shorts or opens

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If missing nets are concentrated in regions with fill cells, check fill cell connectivity to power/ground
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: fill cell causing missing net to power/ground

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If shorted nets are between power and signal, verify power grid to macro connections
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: power grid short to signal net

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If open nets are at vias, check via connectivity in DRC

common_root_causes.cause: fill cell insertion creating unintended shorts or opens
DRC violations causing shorts or opens
via failures due to misalignment or missing vias
netlist vs layout mismatch in hierarchical blocks

classic_trap: Blame layout for LVS mismatches when the root cause is a netlist error or fill cell issue
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: more complex fill rules increase likelihood of fill-induced LVS issues

symptom: LVS mismatch: wrong device sizes or extra devices

first_checks.check: Run LVS and categorize mismatches by device type and location
Verify device sizes in layout vs schematic for failing devices
Check device list in netlist vs layout for extra devices
first_checks.why_first: rules out netlist vs layout discrepancies

first_checks.check: Review fill cell insertion for unintended device creation

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If wrong device sizes are in regions with fill cells, check fill cell parameters
If extra devices are at power rings or ends of rows, verify fill cell insertion rules
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: fill cell insertion creating extra devices

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If wrong device sizes are random and not in fill regions, check layout vs schematic device parameters

common_root_causes.cause: fill cell insertion modifying device sizes or adding devices
layout device sizing not matching schematic
netlist vs layout discrepancy in hierarchical blocks
incorrect device parameters in layout database

classic_trap: Blame schematic for device size mismatches when the root cause is fill cell insertion or layout parameter errors
node_era_note: 28nm: more manual device sizing; 7nm-and-below: automated fill insertion increases risk of unintended device modifications

first_checks.check: Run antenna report and categorize violations by metal layer
Verify antenna rules for each metal layer in failing regions
Check diode insertion for missing or misplaced diodes
Review metal connectivity and via placement in failing regions

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If violations are on the same metal layer, check antenna rule for that layer
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: antenna rule too strict for that layer

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If violations are at the same location across layers, check diode insertion at that location
If violations are random and not at diode locations, verify antenna rule thresholds

common_root_causes.cause: missing antenna diodes in critical nets
antenna rules too strict for process node
diode insertion failure due to placement or routing blockages
metal layer connectivity issues causing false antenna violations

classic_trap: Add antenna diodes everywhere when the real issue is antenna rule misconfiguration for the process
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: more metal layers and stricter antenna rules, requiring more systematic diode insertion

symptom: detailed-routing DRC hotspots after clean global routing

first_checks.check: Run DRC on detailed routing and identify hotspot locations
Verify global routing in hotspot regions for accuracy
Check congestion map for hotspot regions
Review pin access in hotspot regions

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If hotspots are at the same location as pin access violations, check pin shapes and spacing
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: pin access blockage causing DRC violation

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If hotspots are in regions with high congestion in global routing, verify detailed router settings
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: detailed router settings inadequate for congestion

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If hotspots are random and not correlated with global routing, check detailed router version and options
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: global routing or pin access issue

common_root_causes.cause: pin access blocked by other nets or shapes
congestion in global routing forcing detours in detailed routing
detailed router settings not aggressive enough for DRC fixes
global routing not accounting for detailed routing DRC constraints

classic_trap: Blame detailed router when the root cause is pin access blockage or global routing congestion
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: more routing layers reduce DRC hotspots but increase complexity of pin access

symptom: unroutable placement (global placement diverges or overflows)

first_checks.check: Check placement density map for overflow regions
Verify macro placement for tight clusters or overlaps
Review global routing congestion map for overflow regions
first_checks.why_first: rules out routing congestion as cause

first_checks.check: Inspect placement constraints for overly restrictive rules

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If overflow is concentrated around specific macros, check macro placement spacing and alignment
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: macro placement too tight or misaligned

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If overflow regions match high congestion areas in global routing, verify global placement congestion awareness
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: global placement not accounting for routing congestion

discriminating_experiments.experiment: If overflow is at power ring edges, check power grid density and placement keepout zones
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: power grid or keepout constraints too restrictive

common_root_causes.cause: macro placement too tight or overlapping
global placement algorithm not accounting for routing congestion or placement constraints
placement constraints (keepouts, alignments) too restrictive
power grid density or keepout zones blocking placement

classic_trap: Blame global placement algorithm when the root cause is macro placement or overly restrictive constraints
node_era_note: 7nm-and-below: more complex design rules increase likelihood of constraint-induced overflow
